lemmas.note: MERGE of FOUR near-copies (branching E4 for OneBoxRemoval, branching F2 for OneBoxAddition, lr-pieri T0h for HorizontalTwoStrip and for VerticalTwoStrip). One general lemma, four instantiations. Requires `open scoped Classical in` on the statement or Decidable (mu.val <= lambda.val) fails to synthesize (a slip the branching planner hit once). lemmas.statement: For V W : FDRep C G with G a finite group, Module.finrank C (V --> W) = Module.finrank C (W --> V).
lemmas.note: MERGE of branching E1 and Kronecker A4. The Kronecker form is the correct one and is STRICTLY MORE GENERAL: reindexing the character pairing by g |-> g^{-1} proves it for ANY finite group, so symmetricGroup_character_inv (reality of symmetric-group characters) is not needed. Branching's E1 should be restated in this generality and placed in Decomposition.lean. This lemma is what lets a single constructed map Res S^mu -> S^nu certify a multiplicity.

unlocated: neither outerTensorCongr nor outerTensorUnitIso exists: OuterTensor.lean has only outerTensor, its rho/character lemmas, simple_outerTensor and finrank_hom_outerTensor

lemmas.note: Grinberg-Reiner Exercise 2.7.5(b), PDF p.79. IsVerticalTwoStrip is stated as InjOn Prod.fst (distinct ROWS).

lemmas.statement: WeakComposition q n := {c : Fin q -> N // sum_j c j = n}, with a Fintype instance. (Doty's Lambda(q,n).)
lemmas.note: PLACEMENT CONSTRAINT: must live in a module imported by BOTH Kostka.lean and SchurWeyl.lean -- recommend a new SymmetricGroupRep/Words.lean importing YoungPermutation.lean. This is a definition-placement constraint, not a proof cycle.

lemmas.statement: YoungTableau.rowGroup t : Subgroup (SymmetricGroup n) with carrier {sigma | forall i, t.row (sigma i) = t.row i}, plus mem_rowGroup and a Fintype instance.
lemmas.note: Verbatim mirror of the existing YoungTableau.columnGroup (Polytabloid.lean:57-76) with column replaced by row.

lemmas.statement: Theta S0 : (Tabloid lambda ->0 C) -> (Tabloid mu ->0 C) via an orbit slice defined by the S_n-orbit relation on pairs, with no choice of coset representative; and it intertwines the two ofMulAction representations. (Sagan Def 2.9.3.)
lemmas.note: Defining the slice by the orbit relation makes equivariance a one-line substitution sigma |-> tau^{-1} sigma.

lemmas.statement: blockGroup X : Subgroup (SymmetricGroup n) with carrier {sigma | forall i not in X, sigma i = i}, a Fintype instance, swap a b in blockGroup X for a,b in X, and setwise stability of X. (Sagan's S_{A u B}.)
If H is a finite subgroup, U a point of a finite G-set, and tau in H has sign -1 and fixes U, then sum over sigma in H of sgn(sigma) . single (sigma . U) 1 = 0. (Sagan Sign Lemma 2.4.1(4).)
lemmas.note: Reindex by right multiplication by tau: the sum equals its own negative. Same pattern as the existing columnAntisymmetriser_single_mem_span.

lemmas.statement: Top-subset sum: for v injective on X and A subset X with every A-value strictly above every (X\A)-value, any Y subset X with |Y| = |A| has sum_Y v <= sum_A v, with equality iff Y = A.
lemmas.note: Standalone combinatorics, no representation theory.

lemmas.statement: Cyclicity: an intertwining map F out of the Specht subrepresentation with F (polytabloid t) = 0 is zero. (Sagan Prop 2.3.5.)
lemmas.note: S^lambda is generated by one polytabloid; use exists_smul_eq + smul_polytabloid to show ker F contains the range of polytabloid, hence the span.

lemmas.statement: Predicates in the LABEL encoding, for t : YoungTableau lambda and S : Tabloid mu: RowIncreasing t S, ColStrict t S, Semistandard t S := both. These say the generalised tableau c |-> S.rowOf (t c) of shape lambda and content mu is semistandard.
lemmas.note: Working with labels rather than cells (as StandardIndependence.lean already does for standard tableaux) avoids ever constructing the generalised-tableau type.

lemmas.statement: rowWeight t S := sum_i t.column i * S.rowOf i and colWeight t S := sum_i t.row i * S.rowOf i, with the reindexing identities under sigma.
lemmas.note: These two N-valued functions REPLACE Sagan's dominance order on generalised tableaux (Lemma 2.10.2 / Cor 2.10.3) and the column-sorting construction, which is substitution (B) of the route.

lemmas.statement: OneBoxRemoval.rowLen_pos_restrict: for T : Tabloid mu with the largest label in the corner row, 0 < nu.rowLen (T.rowOf i.castSucc) for all i : Fin n; corollary (T.rowOf i.castSucc) < n.
lemmas.note: COMPILED (~15 lines). Subtle case: if the restricted label lies in the corner row r, row r of mu holds at least TWO labels, so row r of nu is still nonempty (Finset.one_lt_card).

lemmas.statement: OneBoxRemoval.card_restrict: (univ.filter fun i : Fin n => T.rowOf i.castSucc = s).card = nu.rowLen s.
lemmas.note: COMPILED (~28 lines). THIS IS THE CONTENT BOOKKEEPING THAT PREVIOUSLY STALLED THE CLUSTER. The image of the Fin n row-fibre under Fin.castSucc is the Fin (n+1) row-fibre with Fin.last n erased.

lemmas.statement: mem_columnGroup_inclusion_iff: inclusion n g in t.columnGroup <-> g in (restrictTableau nu t ht).columnGroup; gives an injection of column groups.
columnGroup_row_last: for pi in t.columnGroup with t (cell nu) = Fin.last n, t.row (pi^{-1} (Fin.last n)) = (cell nu).1 <-> pi (Fin.last n) = Fin.last n.
lemmas.note: The geometric heart of Sagan (2.8). THIS IS WHERE THE CORNER MATTERS: the argument needs the largest label at the END of both its row AND its column, i.e. exactly at OneBoxRemoval.cell nu, not merely somewhere in the corner row.

lemmas.statement: jm V k := sum over j < k of rho (swap j k) (Jucys-Murphy); jm at the last index = classSum minus the transported classSum of the restriction, and jm at a castSucc index is the transport of the restriction's jm.
There is a scalar transpositionScalar mu with classSum (S^mu) = transpositionScalar mu . id.
lemmas.note: Schur's lemma via the repo's spechtEndomorphism_eq_smul_id.

lemmas.statement: (polytabloid (tau . t)) evaluated at t.tabloid is 1, -1 or 0 according to the three cases of gt.B2.
The content vector T |-> (content T k)_k is injective on StandardYoungTableau mu.
lemmas.note: Induction on n: the content at the last label determines the corner cell, because distinct removable corners lie in different rows with strictly decreasing column indices.

lemmas.statement: inv T := number of lex-inverted cell pairs; inv T = 0 iff T = readingTableau mu.
sigma_T : the unique permutation carrying the reading tableau to T; and sigma_{swapAdjacent} = adjacentTransposition i * sigma_T.

Index compatibility for one branching step: inclusion n (adjacentTransposition i) = adjacentTransposition (castSucc i); axialDistance T (castSucc i) = axialDistance (T.restrictLargest) i; and standardness plus largestRemoval/restrictLargest commute with the swap.
lemmas.note: Pure index plumbing, but it is the glue that makes the equivariance check work.

lemmas.statement: beta mu m i := mu.rowLen i + (m - 1 - i); strictly antitone in i on range m; sum over range m of beta = mu.card + m.choose 2; beta = 0 iff rowLen i = 0 and i = m-1.
VANDERMONDE BOX SUM: for b strictly antitone, q! * (sum over gamma in the product box of Ico (b (i+1)) (b i) of vanderDec gamma) = vanderDec b.
lemmas.note: Assembly. Uses the mathlib lemma Matrix.det_eval_matrixOfPolynomials_eq_det_vandermonde, which the hooks planner reported as absent and which synthesis located; the planner's lemma C6 is therefore NOT new work. Sanity check at q = 1: b0 > b1, LHS = b0 - b1 = RHS.

lemmas.statement: D := M - N has degree < m, with D.coeff (m-1) = -m and D.coeff (m-2) = -((m-1) e1(b) + m.choose 2).
indResToTensor composed with indResOfTensor is the identity.
indResOfTensor composed with indResToTensor is the identity.
lemmas.note: Exactly the argument the repo already ran in indTrivialFinsuppEquiv's right-inverse branch.

lemmas.statement: spechtOuterTensor of two single rows = the unit object of FDRep C (S_a x S_b).
lemmas.note: Uses the already-proved spechtModule_singleRow.

lemmas.statement: c^xi_{(a),(b)} = 1 if xi/(a) is a horizontal strip and 0 otherwise.
lemmas.note: With all entries 0, col_strict says exactly that no two skew cells share a column; row_weak and lattice hold vacuously.

lemmas.statement: The horizontal strips over a single row of size a, inside size a+b with b <= a, are exactly the two-row shapes (a+b-t, t) for t <= b.
lemmas.note: If xi had a third row, cells (1,0) and (2,0) would both be skew and share column 0. The condition xi_1 <= a is automatic from xi_1 <= b <= a.

lemmas.statement: finrank (S^lam (x) S^mu --> S^nu) = kroneckerCoefficient lam mu nu.
lemmas.note: kroneckerCoefficient is by definition the opposite Hom orientation; sh.finrank_hom_symm swaps it.

lemmas.statement: Skew-shape geometry: entries weakly increase to the southeast and strictly increase downward; and the skew shape is closed under taking the two 'rectangle corners' of any two of its cells.
lemmas.note: Grinberg-Reiner footnote 769 p.744. Used constantly in lr.BR7a/c.

lemmas.statement: Row-content matrix b i j := #{cells in row j with entry i}; xi.rowLen j = mu.rowLen j + sum_i b i j; T is determined by (mu, xi, b); the content of T is the row sum of b.
M^alpha (outer) M^beta = ofMulAction on Tabloid alpha x Tabloid beta, which is pretransitive with stabiliser the product subgroup; hence it is Ind of the trivial representation from that product.
lemmas.note: The linear part is the standard C[X] (x) C[Y] = C[X x Y]. Using indTrivialIso again avoids ever needing an 'Ind (outer) Ind = Ind (outer)' lemma.

lemmas.statement: Merged base tabloid: for alpha |- a, beta |- b there is T0 : Tabloid (alpha u beta) whose stabiliser is the image under youngSubgroupInclusion of the product of the two stabilisers.
lemmas.note: The only genuinely fiddly step in layer C: an arbitrary choice of matching between the rows of alpha u beta and the rows of alpha and beta. Expect index pain of the kind already visible in twoRowBaseTabloid.

lemmas.statement: colWt T j : the weight of the restriction of T to columns >= j; IsGood kappa T := for every j, kappa + colWt T j is antitone. Plus colWt T 0 = wt T and colWt T j = 0 for large j.
lemmas.note: This IsGood is Grinberg-Reiner's Assertion C(kappa) (p.96) for a straight shape.

lemmas.statement: Column truncation lambda.truncCols j (again a straight Young diagram), the restriction T.restrictCols j, and the gluing of a filling of the truncation with T; restriction and gluing are mutually inverse and gluing preserves columns >= j.
lemmas.note: With a STRAIGHT shape the truncation is again straight, which is why layer A never needs skew tableaux.

lemmas.statement: schurPoly lambda := sum over T : BoundedSSYT N lambda of prod_i X i ^ (wt T i), for lambda with colLen 0 <= N.
lemmas.note: N must be threaded as a SECTION VARIABLE from here on, or the polynomial products across the three sizes a, b, a+b will not typecheck.

lemmas.statement: Call a cell carrying j paired if the cell below carries j+1, and a cell carrying j+1 paired if the cell above carries j; call it free otherwise. Then in each row the free j's form an interval immediately left of the interval of free (j+1)'s, the paired j's are a suffix of the j-block, and the paired (j+1)'s are a prefix of the (j+1)-block.
lemmas.note: THE combinatorial core, and the one step with NO written proof anywhere in the source pack: Grinberg-Reiner p.50 and Stembridge p.2 both say 'easily checked'. Needs sh.bk.rowBlocks in rows r-1, r and r+1 simultaneously.

lemmas.statement: wt T : Fin q -> N, wt T i = (mu.cells.filter fun c => T c.1 c.2 = i).card; and sum over i of wt T i = mu.card.
Module.finrank C ((biproduct V) --> W) = sum over i of Module.finrank C (V i --> W).
lemmas.note: Source-side mirror of the existing FDRep.homFinrank_biproduct; reusable well beyond the Kronecker cluster.

lemmas.statement: schurWeylMultiplicity q shape = Nat.card (BoundedSSYT q shape.val).

Given mu <= lam with mu.colLen 0 <= q and lam \ mu having at most one cell per column, and S semistandard on mu with entries < q, the filling equal to S on mu, to q on lam \ mu and to 0 elsewhere is semistandard on lam with entries < q+1; and this is inverse to the truncation.
lemmas.note: The only nontrivial case is column strictness at a cell of lam \ mu whose neighbour above is also in lam \ mu -- excluded exactly by the horizontal-strip condition.

lemmas.statement: For T a semistandard tableau of shape lam with entries < q+1, the cells with entry < q form a Young diagram trunc T q <= lam with (trunc T q).colLen 0 <= q; lam \ trunc T q has at most one cell per column; and T restricted to trunc T q (zeroed elsewhere) is semistandard with entries < q.
lemmas.note: MERGE: hooks peels the entries equal to q, lr-pieri peels the LARGEST entry in the strip-peeling Kostka recursion; it is the same lemma. Column-strictness is what makes the peeled set a horizontal strip.

lemmas.statement: wordContent w j := #{i | w i = j}; it sums to n and is invariant under the S_n action on words.
sortToPartition c : YoungDiagramOfSize n via Tuple.sort into N-dual, with rowLen (rho c k) = c k and rowLen r = 0 for r >= q.
lemmas.note: Expect friction only from Fin q vs Fin (List.length) casts.

lemmas.statement: GARNIR, in antisymmetriser form. With A' = {column c, rows >= r}, B' = {column c+1, rows <= r}, X = A' u B' of card lambda.colLen c + 1: the signed sum over blockGroup X applied to polytabloid t vanishes. (Sagan Prop 2.6.3, eq (2.4).)
lemmas.note: SUBSTITUTION (A): NO Garnir element and NO transversal. Sagan's transversal exists only to divide a_X = g_{A,B} (S_A x S_B)^-; computing the coefficient of the maximal tableau directly produces the factor |S_A x S_B|, a positive natural number, which is all that is needed over C. This is what removes the whole of Sagan section 2.6.2 from the plan. NEEDS the currently-PRIVATE card_filter_row_lt_and_column_eq and card_filter_column_eq from Distinctness.lean.

lemmas.statement: sigma . t.tabloid = t.tabloid <-> sigma in t.rowGroup.
Coefficient of the blockGroup antisymmetriser: (sum over sigma in blockGroup X of sgn(sigma) rho(sigma) x) S = sum over tau of sgn(tau) * x (tau . S).

blockGroup monotonicity: for S column-strict with the row descent at (r,c),(r,c+1) and any tau in blockGroup X, rowWeight t S <= rowWeight t (tau . S), with equality iff tau preserves A' setwise, and in that case tau in t.columnGroup.
lemmas.note: LOAD-BEARING AND MOST LIKELY TO BLOW UP. Column-strictness makes S.rowOf injective on A' and B', and the descent makes every A'-value strictly larger than every B'-value, so A' carries the top |A'| values of X. This lemma is the whole content of Sagan's dominance lemma 2.10.2. The choice of A'/B' as {rows >= r in column c} / {rows <= r in column c+1} with ADJACENT columns is essential; any other choice breaks it.

lemmas.statement: For x = F(e_t): (1) x (pi . S) = sgn(pi) x S for pi in t.columnGroup; (2) x S = 0 whenever two labels in the same column of t have the same S-row. (Sagan Lemma 2.10.7(1),(2).)
{S : Tabloid mu // Semistandard t S} ~= WeightedSemistandardTableau lambda mu; hence Nat.card {S // Semistandard t S} = kostkaNumber lambda mu. (Sagan Prop 2.9.2.)
lemmas.note: The LABEL-encoding counterpart of sh.kostka_eq_boundedSSYT_count (which is the CELL encoding); both are needed and neither implies the other cheaply. Least mathematical and most annoying lemma in the cluster: mathlib's SemistandardYoungTableau is an unrestricted N -> N -> N vanishing off the diagram, while WeightedSemistandardTableau adds entry_lt and a Fin n-indexed content, and the round trip runs against Tabloid.rowOf : Fin n -> Fin n.

lemmas.statement: pi in t.columnGroup implies rowWeight t (pi . S) = rowWeight t S; sigma in t.rowGroup implies colWeight t (sigma . S) = colWeight t S.
Swap raises: (a) row-descent case, Equiv.swap i j in t.rowGroup and rowWeight strictly increases; (b) column-descent case, swap in t.columnGroup and colWeight strictly increases.
lemmas.note: State the comparison additively (w S + a = w (tau.S) + b with b < a) to avoid N subtraction.

lemmas.statement: For sigma in t.rowGroup, the counts #{i | t.row i = r and S.rowOf i <= v} are invariant.
OneBoxRemoval.restrictTabloid nu T h : Tabloid nu.val, rowOf i := T.rowOf i.castSucc; plus the simp lemma for rowOf.
lemmas.note: Drops the label Fin.last n and reindexes by Fin.castSucc; no permutation of labels, which is why equivariance is immediate.

lemmas.statement: Relations with s := rho (adjacentTransposition i): s^2 = 1; s jm k s = jm k for k away from i, i+1; s jm (castSucc i) s = jm i.succ - s. Derived: jm (castSucc i) s = s jm i.succ - 1 and jm i.succ s = s jm (castSucc i) + 1.
transpositionScalar mu = #{pairs sharing a row of t} - #{pairs sharing a column of t}, for any t (so the right side is t-independent).
lemmas.note: Apply classSum to e_t and read the coefficient at t.tabloid, using the repo's polytabloid_apply_tabloid.

lemmas.statement: For any S_n-morphism phi : S^nu --> Res (S^mu), classSum composed with phi = transpositionScalar nu . phi.

Form and norm package on S^mu: tabloidForm restricted is Hermitian and positive definite; rho g is an isometry; transpositions and hence jm are self-adjoint; joint eigenvectors with distinct tuples are orthogonal; Pythagoras.
lemmas.note: Many small pieces. Recommendation: stay with the bare Hermitian form already in SubmoduleTheorem.lean rather than installing an InnerProductSpace instance on (Tabloid mu ->0 C), which would drag in PiLp/Finsupp glue. Highest formalisation friction in the cluster.

lemmas.statement: An admissible adjacent swap changes inv by exactly +1 or -1.
lemmas.note: Only the pair of cells carrying i and i+1 changes status, since no label lies strictly between them.

lemmas.statement: hole mu m j := j + m - mu.colLen j; strictly monotone; hookLength (i,j) + hole j = beta i for cells; and hole j < beta i iff j < rowLen i, with beta i < hole j otherwise.
lemmas.note: Part (c) is the whole combinatorial content: j < rowLen i puts (i,j) in mu so hookLength >= 1; j >= rowLen i gives colLen j <= i.

lemmas.statement: q < mu.colLen 0 implies BoundedSSYT q mu is empty.
lemmas.note: The cells (0,0),...,(q,0) all lie in mu and carry strictly increasing entries.

lemmas.statement: CONTENT LEMMA: if mu.colLen 0 <= q then mu.schurContentProduct q * prod over range q of (q-1-i)! = prod over range q of (beta mu q i)!.
lemmas.note: All factors are >= 1 because i < colLen 0 <= q, so the Z product is the cast of a N product; beta = rowLen i + (q-1-i) makes Nat.factorial_mul_ascFactorial apply verbatim.

lemmas.statement: BoundedSSYT (q+1) lam ~= Sigma over mu in HS(lam,q) of BoundedSSYT q mu, from the truncation/extension pair.

Corner bookkeeping for the one-box recursion: rowLen of removeBox; beta (removeBox i) m = Function.update (beta mu m) i (beta i - 1); reindexing sums over oneBoxRemovals as sums over removeRows; and every i in range m outside removeRows has beta i = 0 or beta i - 1 = beta (i+1).
lemmas.note: The reindexing is a repackaging of the Function.Bijective witness already constructed inside the proof of card_oneBoxRemoval in YoungGraph.lean.

lemmas.statement: R := (-X) D - C m . N has degree < m, R.eval (b i) = -(b i) M.eval (b i), and R.coeff (m-1) = e1(b) - m.choose 2.
indResTensorEquiv: the packaged linear equivalence, with the Module.Finite instance transfer FDRep.ind needs.
finrank ((biproduct f) (x) V --> W) = sum over i of finrank (f i (x) V --> W).
lemmas.note: CategoryTheory.rightDistributor in a MonoidalPreadditive category. The LEFT/RIGHT order matters and matches: the permutation module sits on the left.

lemmas.statement: EXISTENCE CRITERION (Grinberg-Reiner Assertion A <=> B): a skew filling of some xi over mu with row content b exists iff a family of inequalities on partial column sums holds; and then xi and the filling are unique.
lemmas.note: Grinberg-Reiner Ex 2.9.18(a), statement p.95, solution pp.734-739. SOURCE GAP: pp.734-738 were located by search but NOT read line by line by the planner, so the written proof of this lemma is only partially verified.

lemmas.statement: Assertion D(kappa) in matrix form: the inequality family for T with row content b, restated as a condition on partial sums of b.
lemmas.note: Recorded separately precisely because lr.BR6 is the observation that this IS lr.BR4(B) with the matrix transposed.

lemmas.statement: C(kappa) => E(kappa): if kappa + colWt T j is antitone for every j, then kappa + (content of T on S) is antitone for every northeast-closed set S of skew cells.
lemmas.note: Grinberg-Reiner solution pp.739-741.

lemmas.statement: Ind_{S_a x S_b}(M^alpha (outer) M^beta) = M^{alpha u beta}.
Anatomy of a bad tableau: maximal failing j and minimal failing k, with (b) column j-1 contains k+1 and no k, (c) the failure is by exactly one, (d) swap k (k+1) fixes kappa + colWt T j + rho.
lemmas.note: Grinberg-Reiner p.76; Stembridge p.3 display (2). Uses that incrementing j changes each colWt component by at most one, which is column-strictness.

lemmas.statement: schurPoly (single row of size m) = MvPolynomial.hsymm (Fin N) Z m.
lemmas.note: SSYT of a single row = weakly increasing words = multisets, which is literally mathlib's hsymm indexed by Sym (Fin N) m.

lemmas.statement: benderKnuth j T : the filling agreeing with T off the free cells and replacing, in every row, the free block j^a (j+1)^b by j^b (j+1)^a.

For a complete family of pairwise non-isomorphic simples S : iota -> FDRep C G over a finite group with |G| invertible, Module.finrank C (V --> W) = sum over i of finrank(S i --> V) * finrank(S i --> W).
lemmas.note: General semisimple pairing. Reusable; distinct from br.E2, which is the dimension count sum_lambda mult * dim = dim V.

lemmas.statement: For shape, weight : YoungDiagramOfSize m and any N >= m, Nat.card {T : BoundedSSYT N shape.val // forall i, wt T i = weight.val.rowLen i} = kostkaNumber shape weight; in particular the count is independent of N once N >= m.
lemmas.note: MERGE. Two contents: unbundle the repo structure into the subtype, and show an SSYT whose weight is a partition of m has all entries < m (rowLen i = 0 for i >= m), so raising the entry bound adds nothing. Distinct from yr.L5, which is the same count in the LABEL encoding (Tabloid mu) rather than the CELL encoding; the two encodings are not interchangeable and both are needed.

lemmas.statement: BoundedSSYT q mu ~= Sigma (c : WeakComposition q |mu|), {T // wt T = c}; hence Nat.card (BoundedSSYT q mu) = sum over c of Nat.card {T // wt T = c}.
lemmas.note: Equiv.sigmaFiberEquiv on wt, then Nat.card_sigma.

lemmas.statement: wordOrbit c := {w : Fin n -> Fin q // wordWeight w = c} with the restricted MulAction, and wordModule c := FDRep.of (ofMulAction C (SymmetricGroup n) (wordOrbit c)). (Doty's M^lambda.)
rowIndex c := (rho c)^{-1}, with rowLen (rowIndex c j) = c j and rowIndex c j < n when c j > 0.
Two row-increasing tabloids with equal counts #{i | t.row i = r and value <= v} for all r,v are equal; in particular two row-increasing tabloids in the same rowGroup orbit coincide.
